commits.summary: Merged streams: regenerate the generated trace files, and check only the history of @
commits.body: Two false flags stopped work whenever feature-loop streams ran in parallel. First, every sync.py commit rewrites llm-dlc/index.json, traces/README.md, traces/metrics.json and README.md's session table, so once two streams had committed, run-streams.sh's integration check found the merge in conflict and never ran its script again (foundations, cleanup, application-core and example-targets all hit this; in foundations it hid a real serde bug until the merge), and every merge loop resolved the four files by hand. The new sync.py regenerate rewrites them from the per-session manifests and metrics, which sit in a directory per session and merge cleanly; it leaves and lists any other conflict, including one in README.md outside its index table, refuses if a session file itself conflicts, and exits 1 while anything is left. run-streams.sh's integration check now runs the merged tree's regenerate before deciding, and names what it regenerated in its report (installed by rename, so the running example-targets run keeps its old copy). The merge steps in engine-priorities.md (the worked example) and example-targets.md, and llm-dlc/README.md, now say to run it. Second, check_trailers read every commit in the repository with an LLM-Trace line, including other workspaces' lines, against this tree's manifests, so each stream's commits were reported as 'session ... has no manifest' everywhere else (26 errors today). It now reads ::@ only: a stream's commits are checked by its own commit in its workspace, and here once merged. Verified: new llm-dlc/tools/test_workspaces.py (7 tests, real jj repos with two workspaces: off-line commits not flagged, a bad trailer in this history still flagged, both lines checked after the merge, the four files settled, a README prose conflict and a session-file conflict reported; the off-line test fails with the old revset); test_review, test_runs, test_performance (103) and test_metrics pass. On real data, a scratch workspace merging the default line with the four example-targets streams' @- had all four files 5-sided in conflict; regenerate settled them (91 sessions), check then reported 0 errors once the streams' logs were copied in, as the reconcile does; and the integration script ran on the merge for the first time since the streams began committing (contract 14 pass, 2 skipped for want of a built jvmcontract; test_build, test_pipeline and build.py --plan pass), finding 3 runtime x workflow test errors described in the session. check in the default workspace now reports 0 errors (was 26).
